Signs You May Need Sewer Line Repair

A single clogged sink or tub often points to a problem close to that fixture. When several drains begin slowing or backing up together, the main sewer line becomes a stronger suspect. The pattern matters even more when clogs return soon after they have been cleared.

items: Recurring sewer or main drain backups
Multiple drains backing up at the same time
Wet or sunken areas in the yard
Unusually green patches of grass along the sewer line
Clogs that return after drain cleaning

blocks.text: The next step depends on what is causing those symptoms. A buildup or obstruction may call for drain cleaning rather than pipe repair. If the problem keeps returning, we can look farther into the line for damage that clearing alone will not correct.

Not every unexplained wet area outside is sewer-related either. When the signs point toward a water leak instead, our plumbers can use leak detection to investigate. We also provide slab leak services when the source is beneath the home’s foundation.
Sewer Camera Inspections for Accurate Diagnosis

A sewer camera lets us move beyond the symptoms and see the condition of the pipe itself. The camera travels through the line and sends back a live view that can reveal a blockage, crack, collapsed section, corrosion, root intrusion, or a pipe that has shifted out of alignment.

Just as importantly, the inspection shows where the trouble is and how much of the line appears to be affected. A damaged section presents a different repair decision from deterioration or root damage appearing in several places. Knowing the location also helps keep excavation focused on the area that actually needs access.

Our sewer camera inspections are especially useful when a main drain has been cleared more than once but the problem returns. If the inspection shows extensive deterioration rather than isolated damage, we will explain what that means for the line as a whole. In some cases, repiping may make more sense than continuing to address separate failing sections.
Reliable Sewer Repair in San Antonio, TX

San Antonio has many homes dating back several decades, and older sewer materials can develop problems as they age. Cast-iron and galvanized lines are vulnerable to corrosion, while shifting soil and tree roots can also damage underground pipe. Those conditions make it especially important to know what is happening inside an older line before deciding how to repair it.

Rosenberg Plumbing & Air uses that information to keep the work tied to the actual condition of the sewer. If one section needs repair, we can focus on that area. If the inspection reveals more widespread damage, we’ll show you what we found and discuss the options for dealing with it.
